newsitem.title: JAPAN: Pound surges against yen, hitting 52-month high.
newsitem.headline: Pound surges against yen, hitting 52-month high.

text.p: The yen was left in the dust by yet another currency on Wednesday as the British pound surged to its highest level against it in more than four years.
In Tokyo trading, sterling soared to 200 yen, its loftiest level since October 1992.
Earlier, the U.S. dollar also powered to a four-year high against the yen, trading as high as 123.18 yen.
Interest in buying sterling for yen came mostly from Japanese securities houses and was related to investments in dual-currency bond issues, traders said.
Individual investors, fed up with low interest rates in Japan, are keen to put their money in these high-yielding instruments, they said.
Buying of pounds for German marks by U.S. securities firms also gave sterling a lift, one Japanese trust bank dealer said.
The dollar's rally to 123 yen helped propel sterling higher against the yen, dealers said.

A perception that the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations will not come up with any concrete measures for currencies other than to call for stability on the foreign exchange markets fuelled the dollar's rise, they said.
The G7 finance ministers and central bank governors will meet in Berlin on Saturday.
